title: Ticketing transaction launch certification
goal: Certify the complete ticket transaction lifecycle against the reconciled staged schema without anonymous or cross-tenant money access

in: Event publication, inventory, purchase, webhook, wallet and QR, transfer, check-in, refund, settlement, race, and idempotency behavior

working_set: supabase/migrations/20260926130000_ticketing_webhook_completion_marker.sql (authored this wave; DB-005 precedent migration was the input)
acceptance_criteria: CRITERION 1 — The deployed create-to-settlement ticket lifecycle passes against the reconciled staging schema :: HOSTED-BLOCKED (unchanged, honest). Requires a deployed target, a reconciled staging schema and a real Stripe test-mode lifecycle. None exists in this environment: no staging target, no credentials, and all QA-004 campaign coverage rows are not_run. Nothing this wave changed that status. What is locally true: the lifecycle code path is now replay-safe and the 503-on-a-dead-read defect that made the settlement view unreachable on every active-chain deployment is fixed (see criterion 3).

CRITERION 2 — Purchase authentication, inventory races, webhook replay, idempotency, transfer, refund, and check-in concurrency are verified :: LOCALLY MET for webhook replay and refund; HOSTED-BLOCKED for the rest. Webhook replay was the open P0 in this criterion and is now closed locally: claim is split from completion, a duplicate delivery resumes incomplete work instead of being acknowledged, and the newly enabled resume path was audited so its side effects are idempotent (CP-080, CP-081). Refund replay safety is unchanged and still green. Purchase authentication, inventory races, purchase idempotency, transfer and check-in concurrency are NOT verified here: they need the deployed lifecycle, and the distributed purchase race additionally depends on DB-005's index being applied to a target.

CRITERION 3 — Settlement remains append-only and unavailable data is never represented as a false zero :: LOCALLY MET and improved this wave. No settlement write is mutated or deleted; the append-only ledger and the versioned allocation RPC are untouched. On the false-zero rule this wave closed a real gap: app/api/ticketing/settlements/route.ts read the archive-only `settlements` relation, whose error was fused into the availability gate, so GET /api/ticketing/settlements returned 503 ticketing_unavailable on every deployment built from the active chain and the authoritative money read was unreachable. The dead read is removed and the absence is reported explicitly as settlement: null with settlement_available: false, so an absent record can never read as a zero; the 503 gate still covers the two authoritative reads, so the gate was narrowed to authoritative sources, not weakened. A/B scoped tsc proves the diagnostic was real and is resolved.

CRITERION 4 — Anonymous and cross-tenant callers cannot read or mutate protected ticketing or money data :: LOCALLY UNCHANGED, hosted verification still blocked. This wave changed no authorization logic, no RLS, and no policy: the new migration creates no policy and touches no RLS enablement, so the claim ledger keeps its deny-all service-role-only surface and completion is writable only by the same service-role client that already claims the event. The webhook route still rejects an unsigned delivery before the claim ledger is touched (covered by a test). The negative probes against a deployed target remain outstanding; the venue lane has independently reported the same environment blocker.

CRITERION 5 (added this wave) — DB-008 ticketing code-drift cluster is dispositioned per object from re-derived evidence :: LOCALLY MET, with honest per-object outcomes. Re-derivation did not reproduce the inventory's file attributions in either direction. `settlements` fixed in the ticketing file set (diagnostic proven by A/B and resolved). `track_venue_profile_view`: the inventory's attribution to app/api/ticketing/webhook/route.ts is false; the single real caller is app/api/venues/[id]/route.ts:109, handed to venue. `ticket_notifications`: the inventory's 'unreachable module' verdict is false (the module is live via app/tickets/purchase/page.tsx -> components/ticketing/ticket-purchase-form.tsx:14); only the method is dead, and lib/services/** is outside this grant, so it is handed to design-system. `get_enhanced_artist_stats`: zero code callers anywhere, already fenced by the artist lane's own tests; no ticketing action possible, handed to artist as informational. Honest cluster reduction: 1 object of 4, in 1 file, not a cluster cleared.

evidence: HF-INTG-006-TICKETING P0 CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE, not from the summary: claimWebhookEvent collapsed a 23505 into a bare boolean, the route answered {received: true, duplicate: true} on it, and ticket_stripe_webhook_events declared processed_at timestamptz not null default now() (20260821000000_reconcile_ticketing_foundation.sql:343) which the claim INSERT stamps — so the ledger had no field written at completion at all.

P0 FIXED: 20260926130000_ticketing_webhook_completion_marker.sql adds a nullable completed_at, an attempts counter, and a partial index on the incomplete subset, with no backfill, no RLS change and no policy change; a duplicate claim is resolved by reading completed_at, an unreadable marker or an unwritable completion fails closed with 500.

THE NEW TESTS BITE — 6 independent mutations, each reverting one part of the fix, were run and each failed the expected cases: (A) the original acknowledge-on-23505 semantics fails 6 of 11 behavioural cases including the canonical P0 case; (B) the promo counter without transition ownership fails 1; (C) already-finalized trusting the status flags instead of the revenue receipt fails 1; (D) an unchecked completion write fails 1; (E) a completed_at = processed_at backfill fails the no-backfill contract case and the manifest checksum case; (F) stamping completed_at at claim time fails the claim-site contract case.

RESUME SAFETY AUDITED, NOT ASSUMED: enabling resume inverts the previous safety argument, so every side effect was re-audited. Guarded at the data boundary (inventory RPCs, issuance, ledger idempotency, referral mark) runs unconditionally on a resume; the unguarded increment_promo_code_usage counter now runs only on the delivery that performed the pending -> completed transition; and a status flag is no longer treated as a receipt, so a completed+issued order whose revenue receipt is missing falls through to the idempotent repair path instead of being acknowledged. This last one was found by the new tests, not by reading, and the receipt loss it prevents is pre-existing.

DB-005 REGRESSION CHECK: the replay-safe refund work and the distributed purchase idempotency migration landed earlier (20260921120000_ticketing_purchase_idempotency.sql) are untouched. The only edit to existing tests is two already-finalized call-log assertions in refund-replay.test.ts that now include the new receipt READ; no behavioural expectation changed, and the focused suite grew from 15 files / 120 tests to 17 files / 149 tests, all passing.
